name: W1-consumer-edge-severed
why: THE anti-fake-consumer drill: with the join cut and every endpoint intact, a gate that still passes was never measuring consumption. Mutating the selector would only re-prove the selector

name: W2-generic-question-survives-its-own-answer
old: questions = tuple(named if q == _OWNERSHIP_QUESTION else q
new: questions = tuple(q if q == _OWNERSHIP_QUESTION else q
why: the substitution would silently stop substituting: the agent would be asked to prove an owner gap in the abstract while the owners sat in the message beside it

name: W3-candidate-promoted-to-authority
why: the realistic regression, not a synthetic one: reading the CANDIDATE field would hand 1,162 unreviewed proposals -- 659 of them explicitly refuted -- the authority of the 996

name: W4-lifecycle-filter-removed
new: if False and _owner_exists(root, str(owner or ""), owner_memo):
why: a disposition naming an owner that has left the repository would keep routing missions to a directory nobody has

name: W5-identity-join-by-substring
why: reintroduces T-PATH-SUBSTRING-IDENTITY-001 at the join: path matching instead of a path join plus an existence test, the exact defect W3 and W4 each paid for once

name: W6-distinctiveness-clause-removed
why: the regression drill for this session's own defect: without it a proposal about an espresso machine routes to modules/knowledge_acquisition on the term pair ('institutional','system')

name: W7-applicability-removed
why: AUTHORITATIVE would collapse into APPLICABLE and every mission would inherit all 996 units

name: W8-population-floor-removed
why: a read that silently matched nothing would report the same empty answer as a corpus with nothing to say -- the instrument failure this wave keeps finding one altitude down

name: W9-schema-check-removed
why: a ledger written by a future producer would be read with this consumer's assumptions about what its fields mean

name: W10-semantic-class-gate-removed
new: if False and disp not in SUPPORTED_CLASSES:
why: an IMPLEMENT or REJECTED_WITH_EVIDENCE unit would be routed with EXTEND_EXISTING_OWNER's meaning -- eleven declared classes silently mapped onto the one neighbour that has a consumer

name: W11-duplicate-suppression-removed
new: if False and sig in seen:
why: one concept indexed from several documents would bill a mission once per copy

name: W12-term-budget-removed
why: context economy is a property of the code, not of the inputs this session happened to try

name: W13-owner-budget-removed
why: the materialization must stay bounded by construction against a proposal that matches everything

name: W14-provenance-stripped
old: "  Provenance: %s, corpus %s. These are AUTHORITATIVE dispositions "
why: an obligation that cannot be traced back to the corpus units that produced it is not reconstructable, and a reader could not tell an authority from a guess

name: W15-kill-switch-inverted
why: an override must do what it says in both directions; a switch that cannot turn the routing off is an override nobody can audit

name: W16-outer-failopen-removed
why: a raise in the routing helper would take down the whole novelty verdict on a UserPromptSubmit path, losing the thirteen questions as well as the owners

name: W17-tokenizer-divergence
why: producer and consumer must ask 'what is this about?' with one vocabulary; two tokenizers that agree today diverge the day one learns a stop word, and the join goes quiet with nothing red

name: W18-spec-consumer-edge-severed
why: W1 for the SECOND door. Every endpoint stays intact -- ledger, selector, spec gate, live signal -- and only the join is cut. W1 is left untouched in the same run, so a red here beside a green there is the isolation proof: two consumption boundaries, not one aggregate nobody can attribute

name: W19-live-signal-reads-but-does-not-consume
old: owned = [(o.owner, o.units) for o in routed]
why: the sharpest drill in this wave: the gate still computes the routing and still carries it on .routing, the signal still reads it, and nothing reaches the agent. That is precisely the reader-not-consumer state W5 was called to distinguish, and it is the state this boundary was ACTUALLY in before W6 -- sdd_tier reached the gate and dropped its message on the floor

name: W20-blank-description-routes
why: modules/dataset_first/classifier probes this gate with an empty description purely to read .has_spec. Without the guard every such probe buys a ledger read and a guaranteed non-answer, and an empty prompt is not a proposal about anything

name: W21-spec-boundary-cites-the-wrong-consumer
why: one selection, two consumers, and the renderer must not hand a spec-gate reader 'question 4 of the novelty proof' -- there is no question 4 at this boundary. A shared authority that silently imposes one consumer's frame on another is how a second consumer becomes a copy of the first

name: W22-sm-path-pays-for-the-corpus
new: if False and task_size not in _LXL:
why: the cost argument that held for a rare novelty proposal has to be re-made at a common boundary, and it holds only because S/M returns BEFORE the corpus is consulted. Remove that and every trivial task pays for knowledge that cannot apply to it

name: W23-four-refusals-collapsed
why: an unreadable ledger, a ledger from a future producer and a population below the floor would all become indistinguishable from 'nothing is owned' -- at the exact boundary where a reader is deciding whether to build something new. That inversion is what HR-NOVELTY-001 exists to stop
